name: Hochschild Mining plc
reason: Silver/gold miner in Peru/Argentina whose earnings are set by precious-metal prices; USD EPS 0.39 is the 10y high with EBIT margin 34.4% at the 100th pctile vs 16.9% average.

name: Norconsult ASA
reason: Labour-based Nordic engineering consultancy with a short listed record (GAAP EPS NOK 1.21 to 2.13 since 2021), ordinary 8.4% EBIT margin and consensus LTG of 2%; cheap but not special.

name: Osterreichische Post AG
reason: State-controlled postal operator with structurally declining letter mail; adjusted EPS EUR 1.99 (2015) to 1.96 (2025) is flat over 10 years and EBIT margin 3.1% is at the 9th pctile.

name: Valmet Corp
reason: Pulp/paper/energy equipment supplier tied to customer capex cycles and a secularly declining paper end-market; adjusted EPS fell from EUR 2.37 (2022) to 1.82 (2025) and acquisitions took 0.28x 10y FCF.

name: Neste Corporation
reason: Refining and renewable-diesel earnings set by fuel spreads and biofuel policy; adjusted EPS collapsed from EUR 3.04 (2022) to 0.19 (2025) with net debt/EBITDA 3.1x.

name: COLT CZ GROUP SE
reason: Firearms maker whose growth was bought (acquisitions 0.98x 10y FCF: Colt, Sellier & Bellot) with GAAP EPS CZK 59.14 (2022) to 36.24 (2025) swinging with US civilian demand and defence orders.

name: flatexDEGIRO SE
reason: Online broker whose earnings depend on trading activity and interest income on client cash; adjusted EPS EUR 1.63 and EBIT margin 41.2% are both at 10y highs (100th pctile), so the record is capital-markets driven.

name: Per Aarsleff Holding A/S
reason: Construction/civil-engineering contractor with thin 5.0% EBIT margin at the 91st pctile of its history and EPS DKK 46.67 at the 10y high; a well-run but ordinary cyclical contractor.

name: CVS Group plc
reason: Vet-practice roll-up where acquisitions were 1.11x 10y FCF, ROIC averaged 5.2% and adjusted EPS stalled (GBP 0.95 in 2023 to 0.86 in 2026) while the UK CMA vet-market remedies are a live regulatory threat.

name: dormakaba Holding AG
reason: Access-solutions maker with adjusted EPS CAGR of only 2.0% over 10 years (3/10 years >=7%) and acquisitions at 0.81x FCF; current growth rests on a self-help margin programme, not a durable >=7% route.

name: Burberry Group plc
reason: Iconic brand but a turnaround: adjusted EPS fell from GBP 1.22 (2022) to 0.15 (2025) and EBIT margin 6.3% vs 15.3% average; recovery to 2022 levels depends on repositioning and Chinese luxury demand, which cannot be forecast.

name: Gamma Communications Plc
reason: Strong record (adjusted EPS GBP 0.18 to 0.94, 9/10 years >=7%, ROIC 22%, near-zero net debt) but consensus FY1 is -2.8% and FY2-FY3 ~7%, German growth is acquired (0.66x 10y FCF) and UK SME UCaaS faces Teams/hyperscaler competition after the PSTN switch-off tailwind.

name: Accenture Plc
reason: High-quality franchise (adjusted EPS USD 5.34 to 13.97, 8/10 years >=7%, ROIC 30%) but labour-based IT consulting faces a credible GenAI threat to billable hours and consensus is only 5-9%; consistent with US EPAM/G/DOX (TOO HARD).

name: 74Software
reason: Axway/SBS software combination with growth bought via acquisitions (2.05x 10y FCF), 10y ROIC of 2.8% and net debt/EBITDA 2.1x; adjusted EPS EUR 1.56 (2015) to 2.04 (2025) is only 2.8%/yr.

name: PALFINGER AG
reason: Cyclical truck-crane/lifting maker with 6.9% average ROIC, adjusted EPS CAGR of 4.3% and consensus FY1 -17.6%; ordinary capital-goods economics.

name: Saga plc
reason: Over-50s travel/insurance group whose adjusted EPS fell from GBP 1.91 (2016) to 0.41 (2025) with heavy dilution (shares +6%/yr), negative average ROE and net debt/EBITDA 3.0x.

name: Elekta AB
reason: Radiotherapy #2 behind Varian/Siemens with adjusted EPS SEK 3.76 (2023) to 2.43 (2025), 10y EPS CAGR 3.5% and 5.8% average ROIC; no evidence of a durable >=7% route.

name: London Stock Exchange Group plc
reason: FTSE Russell and LCH are excellent assets, but EPS growth (GBP 1.29 to 4.18) came largely from the Refinitiv deal (shares +4.1%/yr, ROIC 5.9%, 135% adjusted-vs-GAAP gap) and the Workspace data business faces AI/competitive pressure.

name: Telenor ASA
reason: Norwegian-state-controlled telco with revenue CAGR of -5% over 10 years, adjusted EPS volatile (NOK 14.07 in 2024 to 8.22 in 2025) and exposure to Bangladesh/Asia; regulated, low-growth economics.

name: Nexans SA
reason: Grid/HV-cable capacity boom lifted adjusted EPS from EUR -2.81 (2019) to 8.08 (2025), now at the 10y high with margin at the 82nd pctile; a copper-linked project business where post-boom pricing cannot be forecast.
